title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: external address conditions, OR logic and condition testing
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing and policy controls are supported. Minor corrections should expand the two wizard paths and acknowledge that the PowerShell reference documents older supervisory review rule commands despite the product guide's portal-only guidance.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans conditions detecting messages received from external email addresses.
claims.quote: our updated policy conditions enable the detection of messages sent and received both to and from external email addresses

claims.claim: The roadmap plans conditions detecting messages sent to external email addresses.
claims.quote: allowing you to identify specific instances of information being shared with external contacts

claims.claim: The roadmap plans OR logic for multiple conditions within one Communication Compliance policy.
claims.quote: with the new OR condition capability, you can combine multiple conditions within the same policy

claims.claim: The roadmap describes testing conditions with sample messages before implementation and calls the ability introduced.
claims.quote: we've introduced the ability to test conditions before implementing them. By using sample messages, you can evaluate how your conditions will perform

claims.claim: The condition builder is under Communication Compliance > Policies > Create policy > Custom policy > Choose conditions and review percentage > Conditions > Condition builder.
claims.quote: in the Conditions section, above the existing condition builder, turn the Condition builder option on.
claims.fix: Expand the path to 'Communication Compliance > Policies > Create policy > Custom policy > Name and describe your policy > Choose users and reviewers > Choose locations to detect communications > Choose conditions and review percentage > Conditions > Condition builder'. Note that 'Admin units (preview)' appears before 'Choose users and reviewers' if admin units exist. The intervening wizard pages are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-configure, already cited; retain the current docs link for the final control.

claims.claim: The condition builder is selected per policy rather than as a tenant-wide setting.
claims.quote: To use the condition builder, you must first opt in. To do this, in the Conditions section, above the existing condition builder, turn the Condition builder option on.

claims.fix: Add: 'Microsoft documentation is not fully consistent: the Security & Compliance PowerShell reference documents Set-SupervisoryReviewRule with -Condition for modifying supervisory review rules, but does not document selecting the new condition builder or running its sample-message tests.' Retain portal guidance and the narrowly scoped null automation sides; do not infer new-builder support from the older rule reference.
